lesson.text: Quick memory: how often do you test a smoke alarm? (Once a month.) Today: care labels, the machines and batteries.
Care labels: a tub is washing, and its number is the hottest wash in degrees; a hand in the tub is hand wash; a triangle is bleach; a square is drying; an iron is ironing. A cross means no.
The washing machine: sort, load, close the door, a grown-up adds the powder and chooses the programme, then start. Never climb in.
The dishwasher: plates in the bottom rack, cups upside down on top, and sharp knives point down in the basket.
Batteries never go in the bins: a battery box at a shop. A smoke alarm that chirps needs a new battery from a grown-up: never take it out.
Try it in the world: open the practice house, on the Big track.

exercises.prompt: You may take a smoke alarm's battery out if it chirps.
exercises.explain: False: a grown-up puts a new one in.

exercises.prompt: The washing machine: put it in order.
exercises.explain: Load, close, the programme, then start.

exercises.prompt: A crossed-out square with a circle means...
Away for a week, the plants need...
exercises.hint: Too much at once rots roots.
exercises.explain: A neighbour, or trays of water.

exercises.prompt: Cups go upside down on the dishwasher's top rack.
exercises.hint: So water doesn't sit in them.
